latin.539: Tu autem vis illud peccatum esse peccatum actuale Adami, & illius poenam esse non tantum mortem corporis & aeternam, sed imprimis mortem spiritualem animae, positam in privatione iustitiae originalis, & corruptione haereditaria: Ex quo sequitur istam corruptionem nomine mortis hoc loco contineri. Atqui iam probavi non contineri. Quod si Apostolus mortis nomine quicquid poenae per Adamum in posteros derivatum est significavit, nec tamen eo nomine corruptionem haereditariam seu vitium complexus est, ut iam probavi, vides quid sequatur, nempe vitium illud haereditarium non esse in numero poenarum quas Adamus mundo intulit, ac proinde peccatum eius actuale non esse mundo imputatum ad illam poenam, videlicet vitium haereditarium.
latin.540: Veniamus ad sequentes voces ἐφ' ᾧ πάντες ἥμαρτον. Hic magnum scilicet causae tuae putas te reperisse praesidium. In verbis ἐφ' ᾧ consistis paululum, mox iis desertis ad verbum ἥμαρτον te confers. Nempe tu versionem, qua utuntur Ecclesiae nostrae, noluisti prorsus reiicere, quamvis satis aperte prae te feras, eam tibi non probari. Itaque, inquis, stabiliatur & maneat versio nostra gallica, quae est Iohannis Calvini, eo quod, vel quando omnes peccaverunt. Adversus eam tamen nonnulla obicis hoc cap. & cap. ix. quae cum ad illud caput pervenero, Deo bene iuvante, ad examen revocabo.
latin.541: Et quamvis mea fere nihil intersit quomodo ἐφ' ᾧ reddatur, eo quod, sive in quo, tamen ostendam vertendum esse eo quod, ac tuebor versionem, quam Ecclesiae nostrae probant. Interim tu vis explicari haec verba eo quod vel in quo omnes peccaverunt ex prima parte versiculi. At tibi iam primam illam partem extorsi. Si ergo peccasse omnes dicuntur eo peccato quod in mundum introiit,
latin.542: Id autem peccatum non probasti esse peccatum actuale Adami, ego vero probavi esse vitium inhaerens, quid superest, nisi ut illud peccaverunt interpretemur cum Calvino de vitio nobis singulis innato & insito? Ita peccare, inquit, est corruptos esse & vitiatos. Gallice: Or ce peche, duquel il parle icy, ne signifie autre chose sinon que nous sommes tous corrompus: illa enim naturalis pravitas quam e matris utero afferimus, tametsi non ita cito fructus suos edit, peccatum tamen est coram Domino, & eius ultionem meretur. Et paulo post, peccavimus igitur omnes, quia naturali corruptione omnes imbuti sumus: ideoque iniqui ac perversi.
latin.543: Id tamen negas tibi satisfacere: non enim, inquis, dicit Apostolus quoniam peccatum est in omnibus (immo hoc dicit versu sequente) sed, quoniam omnes peccaverunt, ἐφ' ᾧ πάντες ἥμαρτον, & utitur verbo activo, ut significet peccatum actuale, cuius omnes sint participes. In peccato autem originali non peccavimus actu, nisi quatenus in Adamo peccavimus: nam cum peccavit pro omnibus suis posteris peccavit, & omnes homines qui ex illo nati sunt in illo peccaverunt, quia in illo omnes fuerunt. Vis probandi, si qua est, in tuis istis verbis, in hoc consistit, quod verbum ἥμαρτον peccaverunt, activum cum sit, significat peccatum actuale. Reliqua petitiones sunt τοῦ ἐν ἀρχῇ. Atqui verbum illud activum, si significat peccatum actuale, profecto peccatum actuale significat ab eo ipso commissum qui peccavit. Profer, si potes, contrarium exemplum. Vide igitur ne haec tua observatio Pelagio faveat.
latin.544: Deinde te non fugit peccatum actuale ab originali omnes Theologos distinguere. Si ergo hoc verbum peccaverunt actuale peccatum significat, igitur non significat originale, quod tu ipse ab actuali hoc loco discernis. Non ergo loquitur Apostolus de peccato originali hoc loco. Sic nobis, quantum in te est, extorques arma quibus ex hoc loco Pelagium, Pighium & Socinum conficiamus. Sed iuvat te alia via aggredi, quamvis enim nunc quidem meae sint partes respondere, tuae argumentari, tamen mihi temperare non possum quin argumenta, quibus mea causa abundat, ubique disseminem. Dic mihi igitur, quaeso, quomodo omnes homines intelligas peccasse peccato actuali Adami? Inculcas passim peccatum illud actuale nostrum esse non posse, nisi per imputationem. Si nostrum non est nisi imputatione, utique eo non peccavimus nisi imputatione. Quid erit igitur illud omnes peccaverunt? omnibus peccatum actuale imputatum est? Atqui aliud est aliquem peccare, aliud alicui peccatum imputari.

pass_a.539: You take that entering sin as Adam's bare act, and its wage as chiefly spiritual death—privation of original righteousness plus hereditary corruption—so that corruption sits under the word death here. I have already shown it does not. If Paul by death meant every penalty derived from Adam, yet still did not fold hereditary vice into that name, then hereditary vice is not among the penalties Adam brought on the world, and his act was not imputed unto that penalty.
pass_a.540: Next come eph' hoi pantes hemarton, which you treat as a stronghold. You pause on eph' hoi, then shift to hemarton. You will not wholly cast off the Churches' French Calvin rendering—because, or when, all sinned—even while you dislike it and lodge objections here and in chapter ix., which I will examine when I reach that chapter.
pass_a.541: How eph' hoi is Englished matters little to me—because or in which—yet I will argue for because and keep the Churches' reading. You want the clause from the verse's first half: because / in which all sinned. That first half I have already taken from you. So if all sinned by the sin that entered the world,
pass_a.542: You have not shown that sin to be Adam's bare act; I have shown it an inhering vice. Then peccaverunt should be read with Calvin of the vice born in each of us: to sin is to be corrupt and spoiled. His French says the sin here means only that we are all corrupted; the native bent from the womb is already sin before God. A little later: we all sinned because natural corruption fills us all.
pass_a.543: You refuse that reading: Paul, you say, does not write that sin is in all (though the next verse does) but that all sinned, using an active verb for actual sin shared by all—original sin being act only as we sinned in Adam. Your whole edge is that active hemarton means actual sin; the rest beg the start. But an active verb for actual sin means the act of the one who sinned. Show a contrary case, or own that the point helps Pelagius.
pass_a.544: Theologians sever actual from original. If peccaverunt means actual, it does not mean original—which you yourself separate here—so Paul is not speaking of original sin, and you strip the arms used against Pelagius, Pighius, and Socinus. Though answer is my part and argument yours, I still scatter the reasons my side holds. How then did all sin by Adam's act? You say that act is ours only by imputation; then we sinned by it only by imputation. Is all have sinned only actual sin imputed to all? To sin and to have sin imputed are not the same.

539: But you will have that sin to be Adam's actual sin, and its penalty to be not only the death of the body and eternal death, but chiefly the spiritual death of the soul, placed in the privation of original righteousness, and in hereditary corruption: from which it follows that that corruption is contained under the name of death in this place. And yet I have already proved that it is not contained. But if the Apostle by the name of death signified whatever of penalty was derived through Adam into his posterity, and yet did not under that name embrace hereditary corruption or vice, as I have already proved, you see what follows, namely that that hereditary vice is not in the number of the penalties which Adam brought upon the world, and therefore that his actual sin was not imputed to the world unto that penalty, namely hereditary vice.
540: Let us come to the following words, eph' hoi pantes hemarton. Here, forsooth, you think you have found a great defense of your cause. You linger a little on the words eph' hoi, presently, leaving them, you betake yourself to the word hemarton. Namely you were unwilling wholly to reject the version which our Churches use, although you openly enough show that it does not please you. And so, you say, let our French version stand and remain, which is John Calvin's, because, or when, all have sinned. Yet against it you cast some things in this chapter and in chapter ix., which, when I shall have come to that chapter, God helping, I will call back to examination.
541: And although it almost nothing concerns me how eph' hoi is rendered, because, or in which, yet I will show that it is to be turned because, and I will defend the version which our Churches approve. Meanwhile you will have these words explained because or in which all have sinned, from the first part of the verse. But I have already wrested that first part from you. If therefore all are said to have sinned by that sin which entered into the world,
542: And that sin you have not proved to be Adam's actual sin, but I have proved it to be an inhering vice: what remains, except that we interpret that they sinned with Calvin of the vice innate and implanted in each of us? So to sin, he says, is to be corrupt and vitiated. In French: Now this sin, of which he speaks here, signifies nothing else but that we are all corrupted: for that natural depravity which we bring from our mother's womb, although it does not so soon put forth its fruits, is yet sin before the Lord, and deserves his vengeance. And a little after, we have therefore all sinned, because we are all imbued with natural corruption: and therefore iniquitous and perverse.
543: Yet you deny that this satisfies you: for, you say, the Apostle does not say since sin is in all (nay, he says this in the following verse) but, since all have sinned, eph' hoi pantes hemarton, and he uses an active verb, that he may signify actual sin, of which all are partakers. But in original sin we have not sinned by act, except insofar as we sinned in Adam: for when he sinned he sinned for all his posterity, and all men who were born of him sinned in him, because in him all were. The force of proving, if there is any, in those words of yours, consists in this, that the word hemarton, they sinned, being active, signifies actual sin. The rest are petitions of what was in the beginning. And yet that active verb, if it signifies actual sin, surely signifies actual sin committed by him himself who sinned. Bring forward, if you can, a contrary example. See therefore lest this observation of yours favor Pelagius.
544: Next it does not escape you that all theologians distinguish actual sin from original. If therefore this word they sinned signifies actual sin, then it does not signify original, which you yourself in this place distinguish from the actual. Therefore the Apostle does not speak of original sin in this place. So, as much as in you lies, you wrest from us the weapons with which from this place we overthrow Pelagius, Pighius, and Socinus. But it pleases you to attack by another way: for although now indeed my part is to answer, yours to argue, yet I cannot restrain myself from scattering everywhere the arguments with which my cause abounds. Tell me therefore, I pray, how you understand all men to have sinned by Adam's actual sin? You inculcate everywhere that that actual sin cannot be ours except by imputation. If it is not ours except by imputation, then surely we have not sinned by it except by imputation. What then will that be, all have sinned? Actual sin has been imputed to all? And yet it is one thing for someone to sin, another for sin to be imputed to someone.
